Priya: Quick question — I'm trying to onboard halcyon-13b-lite (weights from https://huggingface.co/halcyon/halcyon-13b-lite). The model_card points to a LICENSE of CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0. Can we add this to our model catalog for Dedicated/Hosted? Also planning to quantize and ship a small finetune demo for enterprise PoC.
Sam: NC = non-commercial, so hosting it as a paid API or including in our hosted catalog sounds risky. For Dedicated (reserved infra) customers who pay us — still commercial. For Private (customer self-host) fwiw probably OK since we're not redistributing? :thinking:
Rae (Legal): Correct, CC-BY-NC-SA prohibits commercial exploitation. Important nuance: "hosting a service that uses the model" is considered a commercial use by many rights holders. Dual-license or explicit commercial license from Halcyon would be needed to offer via Hosted/Dedicated.
Luca: Does quantization or patching the weights count as a derivative work under CC-BY-NC-SA? If it's derivative, the SA (share-alike) clause could force us to redistribute under same license which would block closed-source packages.
Rae (Legal): Quantization/optimizations are gray. Many licensors argue modifications to weights are derivatives. For safety assume it is derivative unless the licensor clarifies. Share-alike could trigger redistribution obligations if we distribute the modified weights. If we only run quantized weights inside customer-managed infra (Private) without redistributing binaries, that's usually fine, but we have to be careful about packaging and providing checkpoint files.
license-bot: scanned repo halcyon/halcyon-13b-lite: LICENSE=CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, MODEL_CARD contains attribution requirements: 'credit HalcyonAI, link to repo'. No explicit commercial exception found.
Priya: OK — so short checklist: 1) Do not add to hosted API or Dedicated product catalog without a commercial license. 2) Private deployments may be acceptable but need docs on not redistributing modified checkpoints. 3) Confirm whether quantization/fine-tune considered derivative by upstream. I'll ping the authors.
Sam: Yep. Also flag for sales: if customer already has a commercial license from Halcyon, we can onboard and document license verification steps. We should store proof of upstream license in the customer record.
Rae (Legal): I'll open a Legal intake ticket and draft a standard checklist and template email to request a commercial license or dual-license terms from the model authors. Action: Priya to confirm upstream contact; Rae to create intake and template.
Luca: Small technical note — if we provide only inference via a thin wrapper (no redistribution of weights) and the customer runs it in their VPC, we can probably treat that as a service to a licensed customer, but we must ensure we do not ship any weight files in our repos or deploy images containing the weights.
Priya: Filing upstream ask now. Pinging Halcyon contact: @halcyon-contact. Will copy Rae.
Rae (Legal): Thanks. Also include the exact LICENSE file and model_card in the intake ticket — helps with fast review.
Sam: One more — if Halcyon responds with a CC-BY-NC-SA + commercial license request fee, we'll need pricing/legal review. Flag to commercial ops.
Priya: noted. I'll leave this thread updated. :thumbsup:
